metadata.title: Strong Performers and Successful Reformers in Education: Lessons from PISA for Korea

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD volume synthesises and interprets PISA 2009 results and related OECD desk-review evidence to draw policy lessons for Korea; it does not present an original student-level predictive modelling workflow. The report describes PISA as a large-scale survey with stringent quality assurance in sampling and data collection, but it does not specify the analyst-facing weight variables (e.g., student sampling weights or BRR replicate weights) used in any re-analysis. Where the report cites PISA-derived statistics (e.g., mean scores, shares at proficiency levels, and variance explained by ESCS), these are taken from OECD’s published PISA outputs rather than from a newly estimated model in this volume. Therefore, complex survey weighting and replicate-weight procedures are not documented here for an independent re-estimation, and the weighting strategy should be treated as inherited from the OECD/PISA production process rather than as an explicit methodological choice by the authors of this volume.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This volume is a policy/benchmarking report that summarises and interprets published PISA 2009 results (e.g., mean scores, proficiency shares, and equity indicators) and does not conduct an original student-level analysis that would require explicit documentation of plausible values (PVs) handling. The report also does not describe any missing-data procedure for an original estimation model; instead, it relies on OECD’s already-produced PISA statistics. As a result, PV and missing-data handling are not applicable to the extraction target (no new empirical ML estimation is performed in this text).

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report does not define an analytic micro-data subsample (e.g., grade-only, module-only, or complete-case-only) for an original estimation. Instead, it uses PISA 2009 results as published by OECD (including comparisons across countries and selected indicators such as mean scores, proficiency shares, and equity measures) and complements these with desk reviews and qualitative benchmarking for Korea. Where it discusses additional PISA components (e.g., digital reading option), it reports OECD-published summary statistics rather than specifying a re-constructed analytic dataset.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD report uses PISA 2009 as the central international benchmarking source to characterise Korea’s performance and to extract policy-relevant lessons for sustaining high achievement and improving equity. It reports Korea’s strong mean performance in reading and mathematics and its position among top performers in science, alongside trends since 2000 (e.g., increases in the share of top performers in reading and reductions in low performers in science). The report also summarises PISA-based evidence on equity (e.g., the proportion of variance in performance explained by ESCS, resilience among disadvantaged students, and school-level resource allocation patterns) and on learning environment factors (e.g., student-teacher relations and disciplinary climate). For digital reading, it reports Korea as the highest-performing country in the PISA 2009 digital reading option and contrasts digital vs print reading outcomes. Because the volume is a desk-review and policy synthesis rather than an original student-level modelling study, it does not provide ML model training, PV/missing-data estimation procedures, or predictive performance metrics.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is sparse with respect to empirical ML methodology because the document is an OECD policy/benchmarking report that synthesises published PISA 2009 outputs and desk-review evidence. It does not present an original predictive modelling pipeline, does not report an analytic sample size for a re-estimated dataset, and does not specify PV or missing-data handling for an estimation model. Consequently, fields required for empirical ML papers (e.g., main_findings rows with model metrics, ML techniques, and conceptual predictors used in a fitted model) are intentionally left empty.
